clue.text: Run off one final check, complying with the law

explanation.walkthrough: LEG IT is British slang for running off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something lawful is within the rules, as a legal business is.

clue.text: Burden of son to hold onto love

indicators.note: to hold onto means the boy grips the letter inside

parts.note: a lad is a son
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A son finds holding on to love a heavy burden.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a burden is a weight carried.

clue.text: Get user rebooted with such a handy expression

explanation.surface: Getting the user to reboot the computer, said with a hand signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handy' plays on the hand: a sign made with the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a sign made with the hands to express meaning is an expression with a hand.

clue.text: Manoeuvre scuttles NATO spotters

indicators.note: manoeuvre means move the letters of scuttles NATO around

explanation.surface: A military manoeuvre sinks NATO's lookouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: people who spot and recruit promising performers or players.

clue.text: China welcomes view with no leader being equal

indicators.note: welcomes means the china takes the shortened view inside

parts.note: Ming is a Chinese dynasty, famed for its porcelain

indicators.note: with no leader removes the first letter of the word for view

parts.note: to watch is to view

explanation.surface: China accepts a view with no leadership as being on a par.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is porcelain, MING.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: matching things are the same or equal to each other.

clue.text: Soldiers needing time on track going north

indicators.note: going north in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: spoor is the track of an animal

explanation.surface: Soldiers need time on a northbound route.

clue.text: A few heard about Chaplin's first dirty film

indicators.note: about means the spoken word goes around the next letter
heard says the word for a few is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a few means some

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the comedian's name

explanation.surface: A few people have heard of an early, grubby Chaplin movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns SOME into its sound-alike SUM, and 'about' wraps that round C. 'Film' looks like a movie but is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin layer of dirt floating on a liquid is scum, so this is a description of the answer.

clue.text: Carriage giving church a laugh?

parts.note: a riot is something very funny, a laugh

explanation.surface: A carriage is so funny that the church laughs.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an ancient two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle used in racing and war.

clue.text: Those in charge of soldiers wearing sort of name tag

indicators.note: wearing means the rearranged letters surround the soldiers
sort of means name tag is sorted into a new order

parts.note: men means soldiers

explanation.surface: The officers in charge of soldiers wear some kind of name badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' makes MANAGET from NAME TAG, and 'wearing' puts MEN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the bosses of a company collectively are its directors.

clue.text: Answer by sailor offering forgiveness

indicators.note: by means next to, so the sailor sits beside the answer

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
an answer is a solution

explanation.surface: A sailor gives an answer that amounts to forgiving someone.

clue.text: Piece of slate worn by women

indicators.note: worn by sets the letter for women in among the letters of the criticism

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly, to pan

explanation.surface: A fragment of roof slate gets worn by some women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' looks like a fragment of slate but is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the lowliest chess piece is the one moved first, a pawn.

clue.text: Dirty teeth wobble loose biting end of drill

indicators.note: biting means the rearranged letters grip the letter
loose means the letters of teeth wobble are freed and rearranged
end of picks the last letter of drill

explanation.surface: Grimy loose teeth wobble when the dentist's drill bites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges TEETH WOBBLE, and 'biting' takes in L from 'end of drill'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: from boxing, an unfair blow below the waist, hence dirty or unsporting.

clue.text: Pull a face seeing weapon carried by leader of rebels

indicators.note: carried by puts the rebels' first letter inside the weapon

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

indicators.note: leader of takes the opening letter of rebels

explanation.surface: Someone grimaces on seeing a gun carried by the rebel commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Gurning is the British pastime of making a grotesque grimace, especially in contests.

clue.text: Chicken stuffed with digital application in grand event

indicators.note: stuffed with places the software inside the bird

parts.note: a hen is a chicken
an app is a digital application
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A grand occasion where a chicken is stuffed with a phone app.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an occurrence or event, especially an improvised performance in the 1960s sense.

clue.text: Rewards of victory, plus drink? Misery!

parts.note: spoils are the rewards of victory
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Winning prizes plus a drink, yet still feeling miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misery' is a person: a misery is a gloomy killjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a misery, in British usage, is a gloomy person who ruins fun for others.

clue.text: Relaxing by empty pool must be agreeable

indicators.note: by means beside, putting the two parts together
empty leaves only the outer letters of pool

parts.note: easing means relaxing

explanation.surface: Lounging beside an empty swimming pool has to be nice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something pleasant or agreeable gives pleasure.

clue.text: Pole on yacht keeping dry posterior

parts.note: a boom is the spar along the foot of a sail
TT, teetotal, means not drinking, dry

explanation.surface: A yacht's pole keeps its rear end dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one's posterior is one's backside or rump.

clue.text: So here's a strange sort of fish

indicators.note: strange means the letters of so here's a are made odd and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a strange kind of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small upright marine fish with a horselike head.

clue.text: Misery mostly seen in island's northern blockhouses

indicators.note: seen in places the shortened misery within the island letters

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island, and 's stands for is

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter of the word for misery

parts.note: gloom is misery

explanation.surface: Wretchedness abounds in the island's frozen northern shelters.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: Inuit snow houses of the far north are built from blocks of packed snow.

clue.text: Launch unfinished biography on posh chap

indicators.note: unfinished drops the last letter of the biography

parts.note: a life is a biography
a toff is a posh man

explanation.surface: An unfinished biography is launched about an upper-class gent.

clue.text: Offload one lad by pier after docking

indicators.note: docking means cutting off the tail, so the pier loses its last letter

one is the Roman numeral I
a lad is a son

clue.text: Mate's superior and singular cure

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A friend's boss offers a unique remedy.

clue.text: Place for coach's rudimentary craft

definitions.meaning: a sheltered bench at the side of a sports pitch where the coach sits
a basic canoe hollowed from a log

explanation.surface: A coach's basic vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a pitchside shelter for team staff, and a boat hollowed from a tree trunk.

clue.text: Pat is a person too eager to advance

definitions.meaning: a pat is a gentle tap of the hand

definitions.text: a person too eager to advance
definitions.meaning: someone too ready to advance, that is lend, money, an easy mark

explanation.surface: Pat is described as an overly pushy go-getter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advance' looks like pushing ahead but means lending money; 'Pat' looks like a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a gentle tap is light contact, and the same phrase means someone easily talked into lending money.

clue.text: Leave be, having no end of business

indicators.note: having no takes that letter out of the word for be

parts.note: to exist is to be

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of business

explanation.surface: Advice to let something be when there is no business left to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave be' reads as one phrase, but 'Leave' is the definition and 'be' is wordplay.

clue.text: Network routine with no name

indicators.note: with no removes the name letter from the routine

parts.note: the daily grind is a dull routine

explanation.surface: A network that runs a routine with no name.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pattern of crossing lines, or a power network.

clue.text: Instrument of joy — booze oddly absent

indicators.note: with odd letters absent, the even letters of joy and booze remain

clue.text: Porter seeing soldiers glance back with hesitation after party

explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PEEK into KEEP. 'Porter' is a gatekeeper, not a beer or bag carrier.

clue.text: Cost of upkeep will be inclusive of veggie food

clue.text: Setter upset about bolshie image, that's cool
